arxiv-2109-12181.title: Assouad-Nagata dimension and gap for ordered metric spaces
arxiv-2109-12181.creator: Anna Erschler, Ivan Mitrofanov
arxiv-2109-12181.description: Abstract . We prove that all spaces of finite Assouad-Nagata dimension admit a good order for Travelling Salesman Problem, and provide sufficient conditions under which the converse is true. We formulate a conjectural characterisation of spaces of finite A ​ N AN -dimension, which would yield a gap statement for the efficiency of orders on metric spaces.

arxiv-2202-05127.creator: Shay Mozes, Nathan Wallheimer, Oren Weimann
arxiv-2202-05127.description: Abstract Let G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) be an undirected unweighted planar graph. Consider a vector storing the distances from an arbitrary vertex v v to all vertices S = { s 1 , s 2 , … , s k } S=\{s_{1},s_{2},\ldots,s_{k}\} of a single face in their cyclic order.

arxiv-2203-09643.title: A canonical infinitesimally Hilbertian structure on locally Minkowski spaces
arxiv-2203-09643.creator: Mattia Magnabosco, Chiara Rigoni
arxiv-2203-09643.description: Abstract The aim of this paper is to show the existence of a canonical distance 𝖽 ′ \mathsf{d}^{\prime} defined on a locally Minkowski metric measure space ( 𝖷 , 𝖽 , 𝔪 ) (\mathsf{X},\mathsf{d},\mathfrak{m}) such that: i) 𝖽 ′ \mathsf{d}^{\prime} is equivalent to 𝖽 \mathsf{d} , ii) ( 𝖷 , 𝖽 ′ , 𝔪 ) (\mathsf{X},\mathsf{d}^{\prime},\mathfrak{m}) is infinitesimally Hilbertian.

arxiv-2209-15345.title: A search for new resonances in multiple final states with a high transverse momentum Z Z boson in s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV p ​ p pp collisions with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-2209-15345.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . A generic search for resonances is performed with events containing a Z Z boson with transverse momentum greater than 100 GeV, decaying into e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} or μ + ​ μ − \mu^{+}\mu^{-} . The analysed data collected with the ATLAS detector in proton–proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV at the Large Hadron Collider correspond to an integrated luminosity of 139 fb -1 .

arxiv-2307-12307.title: Robust Weighted Sum-Rate Maximization for Transmissive RIS Transmitter Enabled RSMA Networks
arxiv-2307-12307.creator: Bojiang Li, Wen Chen, Zhendong Li, Qingqing Wu, Nan Cheng, Changle Li, Linglong Dai
arxiv-2307-12307.description: Abstract Due to the low power consumption and low cost nature of transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), in this paper, we propose a downlink multi-user rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) architecture based on the transmissive RIS transmitter, where the channel state information (CSI) is only accquired partially.

arxiv-2311-05636.title: On classical orthogonal polynomials on bi-lattices
arxiv-2311-05636.creator: K. Castillo, G. Filipuk, D. Mbouna
arxiv-2311-05636.description: Abstract . In [J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 45 (2012)], while looking for spin chains that admit perfect state transfer, Vinet and Zhedanov found an apparently new sequence of orthogonal polynomials, that they called para-Krawtchouk polynomials, defined on a bilinear lattice. In this note we present necessary and sufficient conditions for the regularity of solutions of the corresponding functional equation.

arxiv-2409-01874.title: Partial membership models for soft clustering of multivariate football player performance data
arxiv-2409-01874.creator: Emiliano Seri, Roberto Rocci, Thomas Brendan Murphy
arxiv-2409-01874.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Emiliano Seri, Roberto Rocci, Thomas Brendan Murphy. The standard mixture modeling framework has been widely used to study heterogeneous populations, by modeling them as being composed of a finite number of homogeneous sub-populations. However, the standard mixture model assumes that each data point belongs to one and only one mixture component, or cluster, but when data points have fractional membership in multiple clusters this assumption is unrealistic.

arxiv-2410-02367.title: SageAttention: Accurate 8-bit attention for Plug-and-Play Inference Acceleration
arxiv-2410-02367.creator: Jintao Zhang, Jia Wei, Haofeng Huang, Pengle Zhang, Jun Zhu, Jianfei Chen
arxiv-2410-02367.description: Abstract The transformer architecture predominates across various models. As the heart of the transformer, attention has a computational complexity of O ⁡ ( N 2 ) O(N^{2}) , compared to O ⁡ ( N ) O(N) for linear transformations. When handling large sequence lengths, attention becomes the primary time-consuming component.

arxiv-2412-04671.title: Fully Distributed, Flexible Compositional Visual Representations via Soft Tensor Products
arxiv-2412-04671.creator: Bethia Sun, Maurice Pagnucco, Yang Song
arxiv-2412-04671.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Bethia Sun, Maurice Pagnucco, Yang Song. Since the inception of the classicalist vs. connectionist debate, it has been argued that the ability to systematically combine symbol-like entities into compositional representations is crucial for human intelligence. In connectionist systems, the field of disentanglement has gained prominence for its ability to produce explicitly compositional representations; however, it relies on a fundamentally symbolic, concatenative representation of compositional structure that clashes with the continuous, distributed foundations of deep learning.

pmc-11319399.title: Respiratory system compliance during anesthesia induction and postoperative mechanical ventilation needs: An observational study
pmc-11319399.creator: Yukiko Yamazaki, Yuka Matsuki, Koji Hosokawa, Katsuya Tanaka, Yuko Kawamura, Aiko Tanaka, Kenji Shigemi
pmc-11319399.description: Background and AimsRespiratory system compliance (Crs) is a simple indicator of lung flexibility. However, it remains unclear whether a low Crs during anesthesia induction (iCrs) is associated with an increased risk of postoperative mechanical ventilation.MethodsThis retrospective observational study was conducted using a local database. All mechanically ventilated postoperative ICU patients were included in this study.

pmc-11424628.title: Addressing challenges in speaker anonymization to maintain utility while ensuring privacy of pathological speech
pmc-11424628.creator: Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh, Tomás Arias-Vergara, Paula Andrea Pérez-Toro, Tobias Weise, Kai Packhäuser, Maria Schuster, Elmar Noeth, Andreas Maier, Seung Hee Yang
pmc-11424628.description: BackgroundIntegration of speech into healthcare has intensified privacy concerns due to its potential as a non-invasive biomarker containing individual biometric information. In response, speaker anonymization aims to conceal personally identifiable information while retaining crucial linguistic content. However, the application of anonymization techniques to pathological speech, a critical area where privacy is especially vital, has not been extensively examined.

pmc-11500526.title: Screening tools assessing mental illness in primary care: A systematic review
pmc-11500526.creator: Bernadette Neulinger, Christopher Ebert, Kirsten Lochbühler, Antje Bergmann, Jochen Gensichen, Karoline Lukaschek
pmc-11500526.description: BackgroundTo better manage patients with a wide range of mental health problems, general practitioners would benefit from diagnostically accurate and time-efficient screening tools that comprehensively assess mental illness. Therefore, the aim of this systematic review was to identify screening tools that either take a multiple-mental disorder or a transdiagnostic approach.

pmc-11592811.title: Fetus in the Abdominal Cavity After Uterine Rupture in a Primigravida Post-Adenomyosis Enucleation
pmc-11592811.creator: Saki Kamata, Hanano Ando, Erina Matsuda, Aiko Aoki, Atsushi Komatsu, Kei Kawana
pmc-11592811.description: A 35-year-old primigravida with a history of adenomyosis enucleation was diagnosed with abnormal fetal position at 25 weeks of gestation. The patient presented with normal vital signs and no symptoms. A cardiotocogram and transabdominal ultrasound revealed a healthy fetus, normal amniotic fluid volume, and no intra-abdominal bleeding.

pmc-12806263.title: Commentary on LRAs targeting NF‐κB with epigenetic and mutational impacts on HIV latency
pmc-12806263.creator: Shaoming Chen
pmc-12806263.description: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) latency is controlled by factors like nuclear factor kappa B (NF‐κB), which binds to the long terminal repeat of the HIV genome to start viral gene expression. The primary cellular form of NF‐κB is a heterodimer comprising the DNA‐binding subunit p50 and the transactivator p65.

pmc-13063393.title: Impact of Elective Caesarean Delivery on Double Burden of Malnutrition and Its Contribution to Wealth‐Based Inequality: A Decomposition Analysis Across South Asian Countries
pmc-13063393.creator: Maliha Mahazabin, Khondokar Naymul Islam, Md. Alamgir Sarder
pmc-13063393.description: BackgroundThe double burden of malnutrition at household level (DBMHL), which denotes the coexistence of undernutrition and overweight or obesity within the same household, underscores the complex and multifaceted nature of malnutrition. DBMHL is a critical issue in South Asia (SA) and mostly influenced by dietary transitions and healthcare access disparities as well as intricately linked to socioeconomic inequality.

pmc-13146816.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A2258 CHARACTERIZING THE EVOLUTION OF HEMORRHAGIC TRANSFORMATION AFTER MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY
pmc-13146816.creator: Adrian Valls Carbo, Adrien Ter Schiphorst, Richard Leigh, Seners Pierre, Jean-Marc Olivot, Núria Moya I Planas, Abomulay Manar, Maria Hernandez Perez
pmc-13146816.description: Background and aimsHemorrhagic transformation (HT) is a significant complication following mechanical thrombectomy (MT). This study aims to characterize the dynamic evolution of HT from the immediate post-procedural period to 24 hours and to identify predictors of its emergence and progression.MethodsWe included patients from the French MISO and Spanish FURIAS cohort who received MT and achieved mTICI 2B-3 recanalization.

pmc-13396455.title: Towards practical aqueous zinc metal pouch cell batteries via weakly bound water-mediated shear-thickening electrolyte
pmc-13396455.creator: Guowei Gao, Boxin Li, Xiaomei Huo, Zhuzhu Du, Yuhao Guan, Fangyue Lin, Zhenkai Zhou, Xin Yu, Jingxuan Bi, Wei Ai
pmc-13396455.description: Disordered dendrite growth and corrosion reactions of zinc negative electrodes remain critical challenges in aqueous zinc metal batteries. Regulating water states in shear-thickening non-Newtonian fluid electrolytes has emerged as a promising strategy to simultaneously suppress dendrite growth and corrosion for zinc negative electrodes.

pmc-13640248.title: Size-shrinking nanoparticles with high drug-protein payload for efficient, non-invasive treatment of corneal neovascularization
pmc-13640248.creator: Xiaoling Xie, Zhenyang Xiang, Ruhui Yang, Xuanlu Wu, Jinyu Guo, Ruolin Fang, Xingjie Zan, Wenjuan Huang, Yuhua Tong
pmc-13640248.description: Corneal neovascularization (CNV) is one of the leading causes of corneal blindness, affecting millions of people worldwide. Anti-vascular endothelial growth factor agents, such as Bevacizumab (Beva), offer high specificity and low side effects. However, their limited ability to penetrate the corneal barrier necessitates invasive administration, significantly restricting their clinical application.

pmc-13674405.title: Antarctic soil microbiomes encode structurally conserved and phylogenetically diverse beta‐lactamases
pmc-13674405.creator: José Coche‐Miranda, Patricio Arros, Nicolás Canales, Camilo Berríos‐Pastén, Gastón Azziz, Rosalba Lagos, Julieta Orlando, Francisco P Chávez, Andrés E Marcoleta
pmc-13674405.description: Antimicrobial resistance is a major global health threat shaped not only by clinical settings but also by environmental reservoirs, in line with the One Health framework. Antarctic and Subantarctic soils represent a largely unexplored component of the environmental resistome, particularly beta‐lactamases, whose diversity, structural features, and biogeographic patterns remain poorly resolved.
